clue.text: Sack Mark, the troublemaker

parts.note: to sack someone is to fire them from a job
a brand is a mark burnt or stamped on something

explanation.surface: Someone called Mark is dismissed for causing trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a man's name but is the noun for a stamp or sign.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who stirs up unrest or strife is called a firebrand, a synonym for an agitator.

clue.text: Girl looking OK in elfin clothing

indicators.note: clothing something wraps around it, so one word goes around the other

parts.note: fey means otherworldly, fairylike, much as elfin does
licit means lawful, allowed, so acceptable or OK

explanation.surface: A girl looks fine dressed up as an elf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothing' reads as dress but is the container signal; 'looking' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Felicity is a girl's given name, so any female first name fits the definition.

clue.text: Copy Rio?

parts.note: the clue word is spelt R, I, O; reading the answer as R, then ONE (the number for the letter I), then O builds that word

explanation.surface: A question about whether the city Rio is a copy of something.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer is the wordplay and the clue word is what it makes. Split it R/ONE/O, and ONE stands for I, which gives RIO.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roneo was a stencil duplicating machine, and to roneo a document is to make a copy of it.

clue.text: Break for baked beans, the cigar and a pee!

indicators.note: baked food is cooked and changed, so these words are reworked into a new order

parts.note: P is the letter whose name sounds like the word pee, its spelt-out form

explanation.surface: Someone takes a break for a fry-up of beans, a smoke and a trip to the loo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'baked' reads as describing the beans but signals the anagram of BEANS, THE, CIGAR and P; 'for' and 'and a' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A breathing space is a short pause or respite, just as a break is a rest from activity.

clue.text: Legendary rock singer of the 1980s

definitions.meaning: a mythical stone of impenetrable hardness in old legend
... was a British new-wave pop star of the early 1980s

explanation.walkthrough: 'rock singer' runs together in the surface but splits between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the fabled unbreakable stone and, split in two, the pop singer Adam Ant.

clue.text: Collapse of the French composer's detailed inside

indicators.note: one piece sits within the other, which is split around it

parts.note: in French 'of' is de and 'the' is le, taken word by word

indicators.note: read as de-tailed: the composer's name loses its last letter

parts.note: Bach is the German composer

explanation.surface: A French composer's detailed inner workings fall apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' looks like an adjective but means cut off the tail. Strict French for 'of the' would be DU; the setter translates word by word.
explanation.definitionFit: A debacle is a sudden ignominious failure or collapse.

clue.text: Virtual junk food found in tin

definitions.meaning: unwanted junk email sent online, so virtual rubbish
a brand of tinned luncheon meat

explanation.surface: An online snack that turns out to be canned meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Spam is both unsolicited bulk email and the brand of canned pork luncheon meat.

clue.text: Sole gripe about Italian composer

indicators.note: about means around or in disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A complaint about a sole fish dish, set against an Italian composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Giovanni Battista Pergolesi was an eighteenth-century Italian composer of the Stabat Mater.

clue.text: Flintshire village in which pigs are consumed by day

indicators.note: something consumed is swallowed inside, so this piece goes within the other

parts.note: Mon is the usual abbreviation for Monday
a sty is a pen where pigs are kept

explanation.surface: In a Welsh village the pigs get eaten in the daytime.
explanation.walkthrough: Flintshire is a county in north-east Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Mostyn is a coastal village in Flintshire, Wales, on the Dee estuary.

clue.text: Was boob tube part of this order?

definitions.text: Was boob tube part of this order?

parts.words: Was boob tube part of this order?
parts.note: Bristols is British rhyming slang for breasts (Bristol City = titty), so a boob tube is fashion for them; the phrase also means in good order

explanation.walkthrough: A boob tube is a strapless elastic top; Bristols is rhyming slang for breasts.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase shipshape and Bristol fashion means neat and in good order, from the port of Bristol.

clue.text: Acne outbreak on head of Louis Armstrong?

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece set on another follows it
the head of a word is its first letter
an outbreak breaks the word apart, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Jazz trumpeter Louis Armstrong breaks out in spots on his head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Louis Armstrong' misleads: the definition is Armstrong alone, the question mark marking an example. 'outbreak' gives the rearranged acne, and 'on' places it after the head letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Lance Armstrong is the American cyclist, one person surnamed Armstrong, flagged by the question mark.

clue.text: Perfume maker marries big shot, one-off

indicators.note: something shot to pieces is broken up, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I, which is taken off the letters

explanation.surface: Someone marries a big shot just once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' rearranges the letters of MARRIES BIG, and 'one-off' takes I (one) out of them; 'big shot' reads as a phrase but splits between fodder and indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambergris, a waxy substance from sperm whales, was used as a fixative in making perfumes.

clue.text: Where orca savaged Maria's predecessor?

indicators.note: savaged means mauled or torn apart, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: in the liqueur name Tia Maria, the word before Maria is Tia

explanation.surface: Asking where a killer whale mauled a woman's forebear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'savaged' signals the rearrangement. Tia Maria is a coffee liqueur, so its first word precedes Maria.
explanation.definitionFit: The country is a place, a fair answer to the bare question 'where?' with its question mark.

clue.text: Copper's now without a place for suspect

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper, with the S from the apostrophe-s

indicators.note: without here means lacking, so the letter is dropped

parts.note: today means at the present time

explanation.surface: A police officer, a copper, is now without a place to put a suspect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a policeman but is the metal, symbol CU. 'without' drops A from TODAY to give TODY.
explanation.definitionFit: Custody is detention by police, where a suspect is held.

clue.text: Course of oxygen used in case of possible death in hotel

indicators.note: one piece is put inside another, as if into a case
possible signals a rearrangement, one possible way the letters could fall

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: Oxygen is involved in a possible death at a hotel, like the London poisoning case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possible' rearranges DEATH IN HOTEL and 'used in case of' puts O among those letters. The surface recalls the 2006 polonium poisoning in a London hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: Toad-in-the-hole, sausages baked in batter, is a British dish served as a main course of a meal.

clue.text: Hated seeing her bra on wrong model

indicators.note: wrong means set out incorrectly, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the Model T was Ford's famous early car

explanation.surface: Someone hates the look of a model wearing her bra the wrong way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' signals the rearrangement; the Model T was Ford's early car; 'seeing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something abhorrent is loathed or detested, which is to say hated.

clue.text: Distress of a veggie accidentally eating a little rabbit

indicators.note: eating takes something inside, so one piece goes into the other
accidentally means by mischance, so the letters are rearranged
a little of the word is just its first letter

explanation.surface: A vegetarian is upset to find they've accidentally eaten some rabbit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accidentally' rearranges A VEGGIE, and 'eating' puts R (the first letter, a little of 'rabbit') inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To aggrieve is to cause distress or injury, a verb matching the verb distress.

clue.text: Steps taken when throwing up?

parts.note: dance steps, read as what you do when you fling something high onto land

explanation.walkthrough: 'throwing up' suggests vomiting, but is to be read as hurling something high.
explanation.definitionFit: The Highland fling is a lively Scottish solo dance, a sequence of steps.

clue.text: Have a cigarette in the shelter which a tree provides

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind
fag is British slang for a cigarette

explanation.surface: Someone has a smoke under the shelter of a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Have' and 'the' are links; the lee of something is the side out of the wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Leafage is foliage, the leaves that a tree provides collectively.

clue.text: Express opinion on St Ophelia's offering

indicators.note: the words offer up a run of letters lying within them

explanation.surface: An opinion offered about a saint called Ophelia.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts with the last N of 'opinion' and ends in the OP of 'Ophelia'.
explanation.definitionFit: An express train runs without stopping, so nonstop as an adjective means express.

clue.text: Focus on heavyweight boxer's piece of kit?

parts.note: the Ford Focus is a model of car
a ton is a very heavy weight

explanation.surface: A heavyweight boxer focuses on a piece of his equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxer' is not a fighter but someone who packs things into boxes; 'on' just puts CAR above TON in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A carton is a cardboard box, which would be part of the equipment of a person who packs boxes.

clue.text: Bag carried by one old man, in general

indicators.note: carried by means held within, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: A is the indefinite article, meaning one
pa is an informal word for father, one's old man
a grip is a travelling bag or holdall

explanation.surface: An old man with a bag in a general's service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carried by' is the container signal; 'in' is a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcus Agrippa was a Roman general, Augustus's commander at Actium.

clue.text: Are nits mutating and so more dangerous?

indicators.note: mutating means changing form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking if head lice are evolving into a worse menace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and so' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Nastier means more unpleasant or harmful, comparative like 'more dangerous'.

clue.text: Asian republicans face leading question

parts.note: the IRA, Irish Republican Army, were Irish republicans
Q1, question one, is the question that leads off a quiz, with the figure 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: Asian Republican politicians are confronted with a loaded question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'face' is a link: IRA comes first, facing QI. 'leading question' suggests a loaded question but means Q1, question one.
explanation.definitionFit: An Iraqi is a native of Iraq, a country in western Asia, so an Asian.

clue.text: Cutting shows Philip hugging Charlie Dicks

indicators.note: hugging holds something within, so one name goes inside the other

parts.note: Philip Trent is the detective in E. C. Bentley's Trent's Last Case
Charlie Chan is the fictional Chinese-American detective

explanation.surface: Sharp remarks show a man named Philip embracing his friend Charlie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicks' (slang for detectives) tells you both first names belong to fictional sleuths, Philip Trent and Charlie Chan; 'shows' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Trenchant means incisive and sharp, as a cutting remark is.

clue.text: Silver top taken off when hopping …

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter, which is removed here

parts.note: Long John Silver is the pirate in Treasure Island

explanation.surface: Someone is fuming when the lid comes off the silver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Silver' suggests the metal but is Long John Silver, the pirate; 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To be hopping, as in hopping mad, is to be furious, which matches the adjective irate.

clue.text: … mad with violin and cello sections

definitions.meaning: the nut is the ridge at the top of a stringed instrument's fingerboard, and the part of the bow holding the hair

explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link. 'sections' suggests orchestra sections but means parts of each instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuts means crazy, and nuts are fittings on violins and cellos and their bows.

clue.text: English "Times" 71p? Oddly overpriced

parts.note: X is the multiplication sign, read as times

indicators.note: oddly means strangely arranged, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: read the figures one at a time: 7 is SEVEN, 1 is the Roman numeral I, then P for pence

explanation.surface: A newspaper costing 71 pence seems strangely overpriced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' is capitalised to suggest the newspaper but is X. 'Oddly' rearranges SEVEN, I and P as PENSIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something overpriced costs a lot, so it is expensive.
